edges.source: Long-Term Biochemical Monitoring and Dose Adjustment

nodes.description: Prolonged fasting and dehydration precipitate metabolic decompensation and are to be avoided, alongside maintaining a weight-appropriate hydroxocobalamin dose. In practice this is the instruction that matters during intercurrent illness and before procedures.

evidence.reference_title: Disorders of Intracellular Cobalamin Metabolism.
evidence.snippet: To prevent metabolic decompensations, affected persons are advised to avoid situations that result in catabolism, such as prolonged fasting and dehydration, and always remain on a weight-appropriate dose of hydroxocobalamin.

nodes.description: GeneReviews lists nitrous oxide among the agents to avoid, and for cblG this is the most mechanistically pointed item on the list rather than a generic precaution: nitrous oxide irreversibly oxidises the cobalamin cofactor of methionine synthase - the exact enzyme this disease has already lost - so an anaesthetic exposure removes whatever residual activity treatment is working to sustain. It is also the hazard most likely to be met by a clinician who does not know the diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: Disorders of Intracellular Cobalamin Metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Agents/circumstances to avoid: Prolonged fasting (longer than overnight without dextrose-containing intravenous fluids); dietary protein intake below the recommended dietary allowance for age or more than that prescribed by a metabolic specialist; methionine restriction including use of medical foods that do not contain methionine; and the anesthetic nitrous oxide.

nodes.description: Betaine supplies an alternative remethylation route through betaine-homocysteine methyltransferase, bypassing the defective enzyme entirely. It lowers homocysteine and raises methionine without requiring any residual methionine synthase activity, which is why it is used alongside rather than instead of cobalamin.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical onset and course, response to treatment and outcome in 24 patients with the cblE or cblG remethylation defect complemented by genetic and in vitro enzyme study data.
evidence.snippet: Biochemical response to treatment with variable combinations of betaine, cobalamin, folate was significant.

nodes.description: Brain atrophy and white matter disease are near-universal on imaging in the reported cohort, and cblG appears in reviews of the leukoencephalopathies of cobalamin and folate metabolism. The mechanistic link runs through impaired methylation capacity rather than through a directly demonstrated myelin lesion in patients, so the upstream edge is modelled with unknown intermediates.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical onset and course, response to treatment and outcome in 24 patients with the cblE or cblG remethylation defect complemented by genetic and in vitro enzyme study data.
evidence.snippet: Eighteen/22 patients presented with brain atrophy or white matter disease.

evidence.reference_title: Leukoencephalopathies associated with disorders of cobalamin and folate metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Disorders of cobalamin and folate intracellular metabolism that result in defective remethylation of homocysteine to methionine are associated with leukodystrophy, whereas disorders of cobalamin transport generally are not.

nodes.description: Folinic acid enters the tetrahydrofolate pool downstream of the methylfolate trap, restoring one-carbon units for nucleotide synthesis without requiring methionine synthase.

evidence.reference_title: Methionine synthase deficiency: Variable clinical presentation and benefit of early diagnosis and treatment.
evidence.snippet: hydroxocobalamin, betaine, folinic acid, and in some cases methionine supplementation

nodes.description: Without methionine synthase, homocysteine cannot be remethylated to methionine using 5-methyltetrahydrofolate as methyl donor. Homocysteine accumulates and methionine falls. Because the reaction is confined to the remethylation limb, methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and therefore methylmalonic acid handling are unaffected - the discriminating feature at the bedside.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical onset and course, response to treatment and outcome in 24 patients with the cblE or cblG remethylation defect complemented by genetic and in vitro enzyme study data.
evidence.snippet: rare inborn errors of cobalamin metabolism leading to impairment of the remethylation of homocysteine to methionine

evidence.reference_title: Methionine synthase deficiency: Variable clinical presentation and benefit of early diagnosis and treatment.
evidence.snippet: It leads to a biochemical phenotype of hyperhomocysteinemia and hypomethioninemia.

nodes.description: Circulating total homocysteine rises markedly, with homocystinuria. Beyond being the diagnostic marker, homocysteine is itself injurious to endothelium, which is the accepted route to the thrombotic complications seen in the remethylation disorders.

evidence.reference_title: Methionine synthase deficiency: Variable clinical presentation and benefit of early diagnosis and treatment.
evidence.snippet: It leads to a biochemical phenotype of hyperhomocysteinemia and hypomethioninemia.

nodes.description: Long-term management targets numbers rather than symptoms: lower plasma total homocysteine, and plasma methionine kept within the normal range. The methionine goal is the one specific to the remethylation disorders - in cblG methionine is low, so the goal is to raise it, the opposite of management in classical homocystinuria. GeneReviews states the goal as lowering tHcy *and* MMA, but that sentence covers all the intracellular cobalamin disorders collectively; MMA is normal in cblG (see the Methylmalonic Acid biochemical record), so there is nothing to lower on that arm and it is not a monitoring target here.
nodes.id: Long-Term Biochemical Monitoring and Dose Adjustment

evidence.reference_title: Disorders of Intracellular Cobalamin Metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Long-term management focuses on improving the metabolic derangement by lowering plasma tHcy and MMA concentrations and maintaining plasma methionine concentrations within the normal range.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of variants of the MTR gene in patients with the cblG inborn error of cobalamin metabolism diagnosed by somatic cell complementation analysis.
evidence.snippet: The most common identified causal variant was c.3518C > T, p.P1173L (8 alleles). The previously identified deep intronic variants c.340-166 A > T and c.609 + 1088G > A were also seen frequently (6 alleles each).

evidence.reference_title: Clinical onset and course, response to treatment and outcome in 24 patients with the cblE or cblG remethylation defect complemented by genetic and in vitro enzyme study data.
evidence.snippet: Predominantly private mutations were detected and no genotype- phenotype correlations evident.

nodes.description: Impaired thymidylate and purine synthesis in erythroid precursors produces nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony and a macrocytic, megaloblastic anaemia. This is typically the finding that first raises the possibility of a cobalamin disorder, and it responds well to treatment even where the neurological outcome does not.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical onset and course, response to treatment and outcome in 24 patients with the cblE or cblG remethylation defect complemented by genetic and in vitro enzyme study data.
evidence.snippet: failure to thrive, feeding problems, delayed milestones, muscular hypotonia, cognitive impairment and macrocytic anaemia were the most frequent symptoms

nodes.description: Used in some patients to correct the hypomethioninemia directly, on the reasoning that low methionine rather than high homocysteine may drive the neurological phenotype. Explicitly qualified as "in some cases" in the source, so it is not part of the standard regimen.

evidence.reference_title: Methionine synthase deficiency: Variable clinical presentation and benefit of early diagnosis and treatment.
evidence.snippet: and in some cases methionine supplementation

nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic MTR variants remove or inactivate methionine synthase, the cobalamin-dependent enzyme of the remethylation limb. Unlike cblE, where the enzyme is present but cannot be reactivated, here the catalytic machinery itself is defective, so in vitro assay under strongly reducing conditions does not rescue activity the way it can in cblE - which is the biochemical basis on which the two complementation groups were originally separated.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of variants of the MTR gene in patients with the cblG inborn error of cobalamin metabolism diagnosed by somatic cell complementation analysis.
evidence.snippet: The cblG inborn error of vitamin B12 metabolism is associated with pathogenic variants in the MTR gene, which encodes methionine synthase.

nodes.description: Methionine is the precursor of S-adenosylmethionine, the universal methyl donor. Falling methionine constrains SAM supply and therefore cellular methylation capacity, which is the most plausible route from this enzyme defect to the predominantly neurological phenotype - myelin maintenance being heavily methylation-dependent. This entry treats the SAM link as the mechanistic rationale for methionine supplementation rather than as a directly measured step in patients.

evidence.reference_title: Methionine synthase deficiency: Variable clinical presentation and benefit of early diagnosis and treatment.
evidence.snippet: Medical management of cblG includes the use of hydroxocobalamin, betaine, folinic acid, and in some cases methionine supplementation.

nodes.description: Methionine synthase is the only reaction that consumes 5-methyltetrahydrofolate. When it fails, folate becomes metabolically stranded in the 5-methyl form and cannot re-enter the tetrahydrofolate pool that supplies one-carbon units for purine and thymidylate synthesis. The cell is therefore functionally folate-deficient despite adequate total folate, which is why the haematological picture is megaloblastic and why folinic acid - which bypasses the trap - is part of treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Update and new concepts in vitamin responsive disorders of folate transport and metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Derivatives of folic acid are involved in transfer of one-carbon units in cellular metabolism, playing a role in synthesis of purines and thymidylate and in the remethylation of homocysteine to form methionine.

nodes.description: The primary therapy. Parenteral hydroxocobalamin drives residual methionine synthase activity and is the intervention that reverses the haematological picture.

evidence.reference_title: Methionine synthase deficiency: Variable clinical presentation and benefit of early diagnosis and treatment.
evidence.snippet: Medical management of cblG includes the use of hydroxocobalamin, betaine, folinic acid, and in some cases methionine supplementation.

evidence.reference_title: Disorders of Intracellular Cobalamin Metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Early institution of injectable hydroxocobalamin improves survival and may reduce but not completely prevent primary manifestations.

nodes.description: A rare but important complication, and the one with the sharpest diagnostic trap. In cblC it is a well-known presentation; in cblG only two cases are reported. The published case was misdiagnosed as atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome, treated with eculizumab without response, and only resolved once exome sequencing found MTR variants and hydroxocobalamin was started - so the practical point is that a poor eculizumab response in a child with TMA and any developmental concern should prompt homocysteine measurement.

evidence.reference_title: Thrombotic microangiopathy caused by methionine synthase deficiency: diagnosis and treatment pitfalls.
evidence.snippet: We report the second case of MSD associated to TMA previously diagnosed as aHUS in which the patient had a poor response to eculizumab.
